title: Comparison direct image
statement:
Let $u:U\to V$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and let
$L\in\Dplus(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$. There is a natural isomorphism

$$
 \nu_V^*Ru_{\Et,*}L
 \xrightarrow{\sim}
 Ru_{\Proet,*}\nu_U^*L.
$$

It is compatible with identities, composites, and morphisms of $L$.

proof.text:
Specify the map before proving it invertible. By the pullback identification
of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], the counit for the etale adjunction
gives

$$
 u_{\Proet}^*\nu_V^*Ru_{\Et,*}L
 \simeq\nu_U^*u_{\Et}^*Ru_{\Et,*}L
 \longrightarrow\nu_U^*L.
$$

source.place: Proof, first paragraph and displayed pulled-back counit

proof.text: Its mate under the derived pro-etale adjunction is the map $\alpha_L$. Use the fixed finite discrete coefficient ring of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. All inverse images here are exact: [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact] applies to both sites and the comparison morphism, and on constant-coefficient modules the underlying abelian sheaf has the same kernels and cokernels. Hence inverse images preserve lower cohomological bounds. For either direct image, choose a bounded-below injective representative by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]; [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] computes its right derived image by applying direct image termwise. An additive functor takes zero to zero, so this complex still vanishes in every degree below its lower bound. Thus both sides belong to the bounded-below derived category. The required enough injectives on either ringed site follow from [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives].

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: the adjoint mate and bounded-below categories

proof.text:
Cover $V$ by affine opens $V_a$. Restriction to these opens preserves injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives]. Direct-image evaluation and the pullback identification of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] therefore identify the restriction of $\alpha_L$ with the comparison map for $U\times_V V_a\to V_a$. The cone is zero globally if it is zero on each $V_a$: its cohomology sheaves restrict to zero on a covering, so the sheaf axiom makes them zero. We may thus take $V$ affine. The covering basis is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Let $W=\varprojlim_i W_i$
be an arbitrary affine ind-etale basis object, with $W_i\to V$ affine etale
of finite presentation, and put $U_i=U\times_VW_i$, $U_W=U\times_VW$. By [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], each $U_i\to W_i$ is quasi-compact, so $U_i$ is quasi-compact. Its relative diagonal is a base change of the quasi-compact diagonal of $u$, hence quasi-compact by that same node. Since $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ is affine, its absolute diagonal is induced by the surjection $B_i\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B_i\to B_i$, hence is a closed immersion and is affine by the closed-immersion convention. Its base change is affine and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. The absolute diagonal of $U_i$ is the composite of its quasi-compact relative diagonal with this base change. The composite is quasi-compact: over an affine open of the final target the inverse image under the affine second map is affine, and its inverse image under the quasi-compact first map is quasi-compact. Thus $U_i$ is quasi-separated. Maps between the affine schemes $W_i$ are affine (on spectra, inverse images of principal opens are spectra of localizations), and their base changes are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]; these are the transition maps of $U_i$. Pullback compatibility and
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] identify the degree-$n$ derived
sections of the source with

$$
 H^nR\Gamma\bigl(W_{\Et},(Ru_{\Et,*}L)|_W\bigr).
$$

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: Zariski localization and affine ind-etale basis

proof.text:
Apply the continuity of derived cohomology first on $W=\varprojlim_iW_i$ and
then on $U_W=\varprojlim_iU_i$. They give the two outer identifications in

$$
 \begin{split}
 H^nR\Gamma\bigl(W_{\Et},(Ru_{\Et,*}L)|_W\bigr)
 &\simeq\varinjlim_i
       H^nR\Gamma\bigl(W_{i,\Et},(Ru_{\Et,*}L)|_{W_i}\bigr)\\
 &\simeq\varinjlim_i H^nR\Gamma(U_{i,\Et},L|_{U_i})\\
 &\simeq H^nR\Gamma(U_{W,\Et},L|_{U_W}).
 \end{split}
$$

The middle identification is derived evaluation of the direct image. Indeed
an injective resolution on $U_{\Et}$ restricts to an injective resolution on
$U_i$ by the etale-restriction lemma; direct image preserves injectives since
its inverse image is exact. Evaluation of that resolution gives precisely the
same section complex on the two sides.
Fix one index $i_0$ and work in its cofinal overcategory: the complexes in the first continuity application are inverse images of $(Ru_{\Et,*}L)|_{W_{i_0}}$, and those in the second are inverse images of $L|_{U_{i_0}}$. This checks the fixed-stage hypothesis of the continuity node; all the stage schemes are qcqs by step 3. An exact left adjoint implies that its right adjoint preserves injectives: extend a map into the right adjoint across a monomorphism by adjunction, exactness of the left adjoint, and injectivity, then take its adjunct back.

source.place: Proof, continuity display and following injective-evaluation paragraph

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology], the last group is
$H^nR\Gamma(U_{W,\Proet},(\nu_U^*L)|_{U_W})$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives], this in turn is

$$
 H^nR\Gamma(W_{\Proet},Ru_{\Proet,*}\nu_U^*L),
$$

the derived sections of the target. For this last equality use a pro-etale
injective resolution on $U$; its restriction to $U_W$ is injective, and its
direct image is injective because $u_{\Proet}^*$ is exact.
Here $W\to V$ is ind-etale and therefore weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]; its base change $U_W\to U$ is weakly etale by the same node. Thus the restriction lemma applies to both projections used for evaluation. Pullback comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and exactness is [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact] on underlying abelian sheaves, as in step 2.

We check that the isomorphism just calculated is induced by $\alpha_L$.
Represent $L$ by an etale injective complex $I^\bullet$, and resolve
$\nu_U^*I^\bullet$ by a pro-etale injective complex $J^\bullet$. The mate is
represented by the map $\nu_V^*u_{\Et,*}I^\bullet\to u_{\Proet,*}J^\bullet$
adjoint to the pulled-back counit followed by $\nu_U^*I^\bullet\to
J^\bullet$. Each $u_{\Et,*}I^r$ is injective on $V_{\Et}$. Hence
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-injective-acyclicity] makes $\nu_V^*u_{\Et,*}I^r$
acyclic for sections on every basis object $W$. Choose bounded-below injective resolutions of the source and target complexes. For evaluation on $W$, both the source complex and its injective resolution have acyclic terms. The resolution map is a quasi-isomorphism, so [lem-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity-quasi-iso] says that evaluation of it is a quasi-isomorphism. This computes derived sections using this very complex; the target direct-image complex has injective terms by the exact-left-adjoint argument in step 4.
Moreover [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections] identifies its source section
complex with $\varinjlim_i\Gamma(U_i,I^\bullet)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian], filtered colimits of $\Lambda$-modules are exact. Applying this to the kernel and image sequences of the section complexes gives $H^n(\varinjlim_i\Gamma(U_i,I^\bullet))=\varinjlim_i H^n\Gamma(U_i,I^\bullet)$. Each $I^\bullet|_{U_i}$ is an injective resolution by the etale-restriction lemma used in step 4, so the right side is the middle colimit in step 4. This justifies checking the named map on these models. At a finite stage $W_i$, evaluation of that counit
is the identity on sections of $I^\bullet$ on $U_i$. Restricting to $W$ gives
exactly the canonical restriction from $U_i$ to $U_W$ followed by the global
cohomology comparison. The identifications above are natural in these
restriction maps. On taking the filtered colimit they therefore compute
$H^nR\Gamma(W,\alpha_L)$, not an unspecified isomorphism between the same
groups.

source.place: Proof, paragraph beginning "We check that the isomorphism just calculated is induced by alpha_L"

proof.text:
Thus $\alpha_L$ is an isomorphism on derived sections of every basis object,
in every degree. [lem-weil-pbc-basis-derived-detection] proves it is an
isomorphism of complexes. For identity morphisms its defining mate is the
identity. For a composite, the counit is the composite of the two counits
after the usual associativity identifications; applying the displayed mate
formula gives the composite of the two comparison maps. The triangle
identities remove the inserted unit--counit pairs. This proves the
composition law, while naturality in $L$ follows from naturality of the
counit and the coherent pullback identification. For the coherence of the pullback identifications used here, apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback].

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: basis detection and coherence
